criteria.reason: Most claims match CHANGELOG.md and `--help`: the five commands, Node 22.18, the 3-round default, judge B after A, the artifact-change warning, DISPUTED and relative paths; but the claim that every FAIL must quote the text matches neither source, since CHANGELOG only says `record` looks for each objection's quote and the round-1 judge prompt says evidence only "lets the tool and the author find the spot".
criteria.evidence: "every FAIL a judge gives must quote the exact text it objects to"
criteria.fix: In the first paragraph, replace this clause with what CHANGELOG states: "a judge should quote the text it objects to; from round 2 on, `record` checks that quote against the artifact".

criteria.reason: The draft covers every 0.1.0 item from CHANGELOG.md: the CLI and Node version, the anti-ratchet rule, the reviewer's boundary, the merge of two judges with DISPUTED, fixes tied to criteria, judge B after A with the change warning, relative paths, the skill, USE-ANYWHERE.md, example rubrics and the recorded run.

The opening sentence uses `init`, "FAIL" and "verdict" before the draft explains them, because the commands appear only later and the grade values and verdict are never defined; it also packs three definitions into one semicolon chain, so a newcomer cannot read it in one pass.
criteria.evidence: "The draft under review is called the artifact; every FAIL a judge gives must quote the exact text it objects to; and one review, from `init` to the final verdict, is a run stored in its own folder."
criteria.fix: Split this into three short sentences: (1) "The draft under review is called the artifact." (2) "A judge grades each rubric criterion PASS or FAIL, and the overall result is the verdict." (3) "One full review is a run, stored in its own folder." Then name `init` only in the command list.

criteria.reason: src/ does not force a FAIL to carry a quote: `validateVerdict` in src/verdict.ts accepts a FAIL with no evidence, and src/ratchet.ts counts it in round 1 and on criteria that already failed; only a new objection on a previously passed criterion needs verified evidence.
criteria.evidence: "every FAIL a judge gives must quote the exact text it objects to"
criteria.fix: In the first paragraph, drop the word "must" and limit the claim to what src/ratchet.ts enforces, as in the Anti-ratchet bullet: a quote is required only for a new objection on a criterion that passed before.

optional: "The loop runs until the draft passes or reaches the round limit" leaves out the third ending: a DISPUTED merge also closes the run (exit code 3). Consider adding "or the judges disagree without evidence (DISPUTED)".
`criteria[].fix` will mean little to a newcomer. Consider "each fix sits inside the judge's verdict for that criterion".
src/evidence.ts also accepts a line reference such as "line 12" as evidence, so the anti-ratchet bullet could say "quote or line reference".
"drifting without it" is vague. "not converging without it" would read more plainly.
Consider adding the exit codes from `--help` (0 to 5), because scripts and agents rely on them.
